children.name: Amara
children.notes: dairy (cow's milk protein) allergy, confirmed by her pediatrician

resources.summary: Realistically about $1,000–$1,400 a month in new help: CalFresh (~$450), Head Start/Early Head Start child care, WIC food plus allergy formula, diapers, Lifeline, plus roughly $10,000 a year in tax credits. Tomorrow: apply for CalFresh at BenefitsCal.com and call California WIC at 1-888-942-2229 to get the 10-month-old's dairy-free formula covered.

items.name: EITC + Child Tax Credit + CalEITC and Young Child Tax Credit
items.why: Earned income near $22,800 with two children under 6 is in the maximum range for EITC, CTC, CalEITC and YCTC.
items.value: Roughly $9,000–$12,000 refund per year; CalEITC adds the $1,154 Young Child Tax Credit for the 10-month-old
steps: File a 2026 tax return even with low income
Book free VITA help (call 800-906-9887 or dial 211)
Claim both children and the Young Child Tax Credit
Request direct deposit to avoid fees
documents: Social Security cards for her and both children
Last year's tax return if any
items.verify_note: Credit amounts change each filing year; a VITA volunteer should run her exact numbers.

items.name: Head Start / Early Head Start (Fresno EOC Head Start 0 to 5)
items.why: Income about $22,800 a year is under 100% of poverty for three, and both children are in the birth-to-five age range.
items.value: Free full-day preschool for the 4-year-old and Early Head Start services for the baby; saves $600+ a month in care
steps: Apply online at fresnoeoc.org Head Start 0 to 5
Ask for Early Head Start for the 10-month-old
Bring income and birth documents to the enrollment appointment
Tell staff about the milk allergy for the meal plan
items.verify_note: Openings vary by center; ask to be put on the waiting list for the nearest 93702 site.
items.source_quote: Children from birth to age five who are from families with incomes below the poverty guidelines are eligible for Head Start services.

items.name: CalFresh (SNAP in California)
items.why: Her $1,900 a month is far under the CalFresh gross limit for a household of three, and California has no asset test.
items.value: About $400–$550 a month on an EBT card, plus free school and summer meal links
steps: Apply at BenefitsCal.com for Fresno County
Upload pay stubs and ID in the portal
Answer the phone interview call within 30 days
Report rent and utility costs to raise the benefit
items.verify_note: Final amount depends on rent and utilities; ask the worker for expedited service if she has under $150 cash.
items.source_quote: Most CalFresh households are subject to a gross income determination test. ... The maximum gross allowed is 200% of the Federal poverty level (FPL).

items.name: Medi-Cal (Medicaid in California)
items.why: She is already enrolled. Keep it active; it also opens doors to WIC, Lifeline and utility discounts.
items.value: Free doctor visits, allergy specialist, prescriptions and dental for all three; worth $300+ a month
steps: Keep her address current with Fresno County so renewal mail arrives
Return the yearly renewal packet on time
Ask the pediatrician for an allergy specialist referral
Request transportation to appointments, a covered Medi-Cal benefit
items.verify_note: Already enrolled. Confirm the baby and the 4-year-old are both on the case, not just her.

items.name: California WIC (Women, Infants and Children)
items.why: Income under $4,212 a month for three qualifies, and Medi-Cal enrollment makes her automatically income-eligible.
items.value: About $120 a month in food benefits for two children, plus prescribed dairy-free formula for the baby
steps: Call 1-888-942-2229 to book a Fresno WIC appointment
Ask for a medical formula request form for the milk allergy
Have the pediatrician document the cow's milk protein allergy
Load benefits on the WIC card and shop at approved stores
items.verify_note: Specialty formula needs the doctor's written medical documentation; WIC decides which brands it covers.
items.source_quote: WIC INCOME GUIDELINES ... Gross Income 185% Federal Poverty Level ... 3 · $50,542 · $4,212 · $2,106 · $1,944 · $972

items.name: Central California Food Bank diaper program (NDBN member, Fresno)
items.why: It is the National Diaper Bank Network member serving Fresno; distributions are open to local low-income families.
items.value: Free diapers and wipes each month, worth about $40–$70
steps: Call the Central California Food Bank for the diaper distribution schedule
Go to the nearest 93702 distribution site
Bring the baby's size and age
Pick up groceries at the same visit
documents: Child's birth certificate or Medi-Cal card
items.verify_note: Diaper supply is limited and site-based; confirm the current day and location by phone.

items.name: California LifeLine (discount phone and internet)
items.why: Medi-Cal enrollment qualifies a household for LifeLine; one discount per household.
items.value: Free or near-free cell service; often $20–$40 a month saved
steps: Pick a LifeLine carrier at californialifeline.com
Apply through the carrier using her Medi-Cal enrollment
Return the PIN letter from the LifeLine administrator by the deadline
Ask the carrier about low-cost home internet too
items.verify_note: Income and program rules were not verified today; confirm current qualifying programs on the LifeLine site.

items.name: LIHEAP energy bill help (Fresno EOC Energy Services)
items.why: Fresno County residents under 60% of state median income get one energy payment per program year.
items.value: One payment toward the power or gas bill, up to $3,000; plus CARE rate discount of 20–35%
steps: Apply online through Fresno EOC Energy Services
Upload six weeks of pay stubs and the full energy bill
Ask about free weatherization at the same time
Call PG&E separately to enroll in CARE
documents: Pay stubs for the last six weeks
All pages of the current energy bill
items.verify_note: Paper applications ended; applications are online only and funds run out during the year.
items.source_quote: Heating, Cooling, Crisis, & Weatherization: 60% State Median Income

items.name: 211 Fresno County, food pantries and free baby goods
items.why: 211 is open to everyone and routes by ZIP to pantries, rent help and baby supply closets near 93702.
items.value: Free groceries weekly, clothing, car seats, holiday help; easily $100+ a month in goods
steps: Dial 211 and give ZIP 93702
Ask for the closest weekly food pantry and baby supply closet
Join a Fresno Buy Nothing group on Facebook for free clothes and gear
Ask the library about free storytime and Reach Out and Read books
documents: Number of people in the household
items.verify_note: Pantry hours change often; call 211 the same week before going.

items.name: California child care subsidy (CCDF / Alternative Payment Program, Fresno)
items.why: Her income is well under the state ceiling, but Fresno subsidy slots are limited and run from a waiting list.
items.value: Free or low-cost licensed child care or a paid relative provider; worth $300–$800 a month
steps: Join the Fresno County centralized eligibility list for child care
Submit income and work or school schedule
Choose a licensed provider or an approved family member
Recheck the waitlist every 60 days
items.verify_note: The correct Fresno intake agency and current income ceiling were not confirmed today; call 211 for the local resource and referral agency.

items.name: CalWORKs (TANF cash aid in California)
items.why: Applicants subtract $450 per worker from earnings, then compare to the MBSAC limit; $1,450 may be just over the limit for three.
items.value: Monthly cash aid plus automatic child care and Head Start eligibility if approved
steps: Apply on BenefitsCal.com at the same time as CalFresh
Report all earned income honestly
Ask the worker to run the MBSAC applicant test
Ask about one-time Homeless Assistance or diversion payment if behind on rent
items.verify_note: The 2026 MBSAC figure for a family of three was not confirmed; let the county test it rather than assume she is over.
items.source_quote: Subtract $450 of earned income for each working family member

items.name: Early Start (IDEA Part C) through Central Valley Regional Center
items.why: Free evaluation for any baby under 3 with a developmental or medical concern; a food allergy alone may not qualify.
items.value: Free developmental evaluation, feeding and nutrition support, therapy if a delay is found
steps: Call the Early Start BabyLine at 800-515-2229
Ask the pediatrician to fax a referral for feeding concerns
Accept the free evaluation within 45 days
Ask about WIC and nutrition follow-up if a feeding issue is found
documents: Pediatrician's notes on the milk allergy
items.verify_note: Eligibility needs a 25% delay or an established risk condition; the evaluation itself is free either way.
items.source_quote: To request an assessment for Early Start services, start by contacting the regional center in your county.
